create-analysis.header.title: Create analysis
create-analysis.header.description: Configure your database analysis to receive intelligent recommendations for modernizing to AWS purpose-built databases.
create-analysis.form.analysis-mode.label: Analysis mode
create-analysis.form.analysis-mode.descr: Choose between online mode (connect to live database) or offline mode (use pre-collected data)
create-analysis.form.analysis-mode.onlin: Connect directly to your database for real-time analysis
create-analysis.form.analysis-mode.offli: Analyze pre-collected database metadata from S3
create-analysis.step.source-database.des: Specify the source database connection details
create-analysis.source.rds-instance.desc: Select an existing RDS instance from your account or enter connection details manually below.
create-analysis.source.host.label: Host
create-analysis.source.host.description: Enter the database endpoint or hostname.
create-analysis.source.host.constraint-t: Enter a valid hostname or IP address.
create-analysis.source.port.label: Port
create-analysis.source.database-name.des: Enter the name of the database to analyze.
create-analysis.source.database-name.con: Letters, digits, _ and -, up to 128 characters.
create-analysis.source.credentials.label: Credentials
create-analysis.source.credentials.descr: Store the database username and password in AWS Secrets Manager (or another secrets manager), then enter the secret ARN or name. Passwords are never entered or sent here.
create-analysis.source.secret-arn.label: Secret ARN
create-analysis.source.secret-arn.constr: Enter the full ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing database credentials.
create-analysis.source.secret-name.label: Secret name
create-analysis.source.secret-name.const: Enter the name of the AWS Secrets Manager secret.
create-analysis.collection.anonymize-pii: Automatically anonymize personally identifiable information in collected data to protect sensitive information.
create-analysis.collection.include-sampl: Collect sample data from tables to enable more accurate recommendations for data modeling and access patterns.
create-analysis.collection.sample-size.d: Number of rows to sample from each table. Larger samples provide more accurate analysis but take longer to collect.
create-analysis.collection.sample-size.c: Choose between 100 and 10,000 rows per table.
create-analysis.collection.query-log-per: Number of days of query history to analyze. Longer periods provide better workload understanding but take more time to process.
create-analysis.collection.query-log-sou: Select the source for collecting query performance data. Performance Insights provides the most detailed analysis.
create-analysis.target-databases.label: Select target databases for analysis
create-analysis.target-databases.descrip: Choose one or more databases to evaluate. The system will analyze your workload and provide specific recommendations for each selected database type.
create-analysis.target-databases.dynamod: Key-value and document database for high-throughput workloads.
create-analysis.target-databases.documen: MongoDB-compatible database service for JSON workloads.
create-analysis.target-databases.elastic: In-memory caching service supporting Redis and Memcached.
create-analysis.target-databases.opensea: Search and analytics engine for log analytics and full-text search.
create-analysis.target-databases.neptune: Graph database service for highly connected datasets. (Coming soon)
create-analysis.target-databases.aurora-: MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database. (Coming soon)
create-analysis.advanced.include-pattern: Specify patterns for tables to include in the analysis. Leave empty to include all tables.
Enter comma-separated patterns. Use % as wildcard. Example: user_%, prod_%
create-analysis.advanced.exclude-pattern: Specify patterns for tables to exclude from the analysis. Excluded tables will not be analyzed.
Enter comma-separated patterns. Use % as wildcard. Example: temp_%, test_%
create-analysis.advanced.performance-ins: Configure which Performance Insights metrics to collect for workload analysis.
create-analysis.advanced.cloudwatch.desc: Select which CloudWatch metrics to collect for cost and performance analysis.
create-analysis.advanced.custom-query-pa: Define custom SQL query patterns to analyze in addition to the collected queries.
Enter one query pattern per line. Use SQL LIKE syntax with % wildcards.
create-analysis.advanced.collection-inte: Specify custom interval in minutes for collecting Performance Insights data. Default is 60 minutes.
Enter a value between 1 and 1440 minutes.
create-analysis.offline.database-info.so: Engine type of the source database

settings.header.title: Settings
settings.header.description: Configure system settings including AWS resources, default analysis parameters, and user interface preferences. Changes will be applied to future analyses.
settings.aws-config.header.title: AWS configuration
settings.aws-config.header.description: Configure AWS resources used by the Database Modernizer Assessment Tool for storing analysis results and intermediate data.
settings.aws-config.region.label: Default AWS Region
settings.aws-config.region.description: Select the AWS Region where analysis results and intermediate data will be stored. This region will be used as the default for all new analyses.
settings.aws-config.region.constraint-te: The region must support the required AWS services: S3, DynamoDB, and Performance Insights.
settings.aws-config.s3-bucket.label: S3 bucket for results
settings.aws-config.s3-bucket.descriptio: Specify the S3 bucket where analysis results, collector output, and generated reports will be stored. The bucket must exist in the selected region.
settings.aws-config.s3-bucket.constraint: Enter a valid S3 bucket name. Bucket names must be between 3 and 63 characters long and can contain only lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and periods.
settings.aws-config.dynamodb-table.label: DynamoDB table name
settings.aws-config.dynamodb-table.descr: Specify the DynamoDB table used to store job metadata, execution history, and analysis state information. The table will be created automatically if it doesn't exist.
settings.aws-config.dynamodb-table.const: Enter a valid DynamoDB table name. Table names must be between 3 and 255 characters long and can contain only letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens, and periods.
settings.aws-config.iam-role.label: IAM execution role - optional
settings.aws-config.iam-role.description: Specify an IAM role that the Database Modernizer Assessment Tool will assume when performing analyses. If not specified, the service will use the default execution role.
settings.aws-config.iam-role.constraint-: Enter a valid IAM role ARN in the format: arn:aws:iam::account-id:role/role-name
settings.analysis-options.header.title: Default analysis options
settings.analysis-options.header.descrip: Set default parameters for new database analyses. These values will be pre-populated when creating a new analysis.
settings.analysis-options.query-log-peri: Set the default number of days of query history to analyze for new analyses.
settings.analysis-options.sample-size.de: Set the default number of rows to sample from each table for new analyses.
settings.analysis-options.sample-size.co: Choose between 100 and 10,000 rows per table.
settings.analysis-options.target-databas: Select which AWS purpose-built databases should be pre-selected by default for new analyses.
NoSQL key-value and document database for high-scale applications.
MongoDB-compatible database service for JSON workloads.
In-memory caching service supporting Redis and Memcached.
Search and analytics engine for log analytics and full-text search.
Graph database service for highly connected datasets.
Apache Cassandra-compatible database service for wide-column workloads.
MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database with cloud optimizations.
settings.analysis-options.pii-anonymizat: Set whether PII anonymization should be enabled by default for new analyses.
Automatically anonymize personally identifiable information in collected data to protect sensitive information.
settings.analysis-options.sample-data.de: Set whether sample data collection should be enabled by default for new analyses.
settings.analysis-options.sample-data.ch: Collect sample data from tables to enable more accurate recommendations for data modeling and access patterns.
settings.ui-preferences.header.title: UI preferences
settings.ui-preferences.header.descripti: Customize your user interface experience including theme, refresh behavior, and notification settings.
settings.ui-preferences.color-theme.desc: Choose the color theme for the Database Modernizer Assessment Tool interface. The system default option will match your operating system settings.
settings.ui-preferences.auto-refresh.des: Set how frequently the dashboard and job monitoring pages automatically refresh to show the latest data.
settings.ui-preferences.auto-refresh.con: Choose an interval between 5 seconds and 5 minutes, or disable auto-refresh.
settings.ui-preferences.browser-notifica: Enable browser notifications to receive alerts when analysis jobs complete, fail, or require attention.
You may need to grant browser notification permissions when enabled.
settings.ui-preferences.email-notificati: Receive email notifications for important events related to your database analyses.
Email notifications will be sent to your account email address.
settings.ui-preferences.notification-eve: Select which events should trigger notifications when browser or email notifications are enabled.
Receive notifications when analysis jobs complete successfully.
Receive notifications when analysis jobs fail or encounter errors.
Receive notifications when analysis jobs complete with warnings.
Receive notifications when analysis jobs exceed expected duration.
settings.ui-preferences.compact-mode.des: Choose between comfortable and compact display modes for tables and lists throughout the interface.
settings.ui-preferences.compact-mode.tog: Enable to display more items on screen with reduced spacing.

analysis-results.sources-of-truth.intro: Each table's writes land on one engine, its source of truth. An engine that serves the table's reads keeps a copy in sync from it via CDC, so those reads are eventually consistent.
analysis-results.sources-of-truth.risk-l: Every table above has this risk.
Every other table above has this risk.
analysis-results.sources-of-truth.risk-o: Eventually consistent: a read on a replica reads a copy kept in sync from {{source}} via CDC, so it sees a write only after CDC applies it, behind by the replication lag; a read that must see its own write should read from {{source}}.
analysis-results.sources-of-truth.risk-m: Eventually consistent: a read on a replica reads a copy kept in sync from its source of truth ({{sources}} or {{last}}) via CDC, so it sees a write only after CDC applies it, behind by the replication lag; a read that must see its own write should read from the source of truth.
analysis-results.sources-of-truth.more_o: {{count}} more replicated table is listed in the Assessment Data (JSON), under table_sources.

analysis-results.unservable.header_other: {{count}} queries that cannot be served as designed
analysis-results.unservable.intro: These queries cannot be served as designed on the engine they are on. The assessment does not bring back an engine it removed: keep each query where it is, or redesign it, then re-run.
analysis-results.unservable.fallback_all: These landed on a fallback engine because no analyzed engine could take them: it runs the query, but no analysis scored it there and no design covers it.
analysis-results.unservable.fallback_som: Some landed on a fallback engine because no analyzed engine could take them: it runs the query, but no analysis scored it there and no design covers it.
analysis-results.unservable.flagged_all: These were scored and designed on their engine, then a review found that engine cannot serve them, and no other engine the plan keeps can take them, so they stay there.
analysis-results.unservable.flagged_some: Some were scored and designed on their engine, then a review found that engine cannot serve them, and no other engine the plan keeps can take them, so they stay there.
analysis-results.unservable.held_all: These were scored and designed on their engine, then a design review found that engine cannot serve them. A write on each query's table is pinned to that engine in the assignment review, and a table has one writer, so they stay there until the pin changes.
analysis-results.unservable.held_some: Some were scored and designed on their engine, then a design review found that engine cannot serve them. A write on each query's table is pinned to that engine in the assignment review, and a table has one writer, so they stay there until the pin changes.
